mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.1% compresses equity discount rates through accommodative monetary policy, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days. This mechanism activates whenever FEDFUNDS remains at or below 0.1%.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 0.1% signals aggressive monetary tightening, raising equity discount rates and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.1% in the last month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 40% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises above 0.1%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous strength in housing starts (HOUST > 1100) and retail sales (RSAFS > 430,000) indicates robust consumer demand, driving corporate earnings growth and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of periods when HOUST > 1100 and RSAFS > 430000.

mechanism_narrative: High unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%) signals economic weakness, triggering central bank stimulus and fiscal support that drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of periods when UNRATE > 6.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO > 100) indicates expanding manufacturing output, supporting corporate earnings growth and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in > 40% of periods when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts below 1000 units signals weak consumer demand and potential economic slowdown, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in > 40% of periods when HOUST < 1000.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 235) and rising federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS increase > 0.05% in 3 months) signals aggressive monetary tightening, depressing equity valuations and causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 235 and FEDFUNDS increases > 0.05% in 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 40% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 235 and FEDFUNDS increases > 0.05% in 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion (annualized GDP growth > 2%), overheating risks prompt monetary tightening, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in > 40% of periods when annualized GDP growth > 2%.
